# task-4b8fb79e: horizontal-run count encoding

## Rule / evidence
The input is a sparse grid containing horizontal runs of two foreground colors (demonstrations use 3 and 2) over a uniform background. Each maximal horizontal contiguous run is one item, regardless of its length or position. Count the runs of each foreground color. Return a 2×3 output, with color 3 in the first row and color 2 in the second row: fill cells left-to-right with that color for each run, then pad remaining cells with 0. (The observed count capacity is three per color.)

Demo 1: input had four separate runs of 3 (lengths 6, 8, 4, 3) and one run of 2 (length 4); output [[3,3,3],[3,2,0]].

Demo 2: input had two runs of 3 (both length 4) and two runs of 2 (lengths 2 and 3); output [[3,3,2],[2,0,0]].

Test: input had three runs of 3 (lengths 4,4,2) and three of 2 (lengths 6,2,4); output [[3,3,3],[2,2,2]] was accepted.

## Pitfalls
- Count disconnected horizontal components/runs, not individual cells and not total bar lengths.
- Ignore background and the runs' coordinates/ordering; output groups counts by color, 3 row first and 2 row second.
- Handle runs in different rows and multiple runs on the same row independently. Use maximal contiguous runs; separated same-color bars are distinct.
- Recheck whether colors/layout differ on a recurrence; infer the two foreground colors and output ordering from demonstrations rather than assuming these exact values universally."
}
